title: One of my most anticipated shows of the Spring- but did it live up to...
transcript: Steve Carell is making his Broadway debut in Uncle Vanya. But how is it so? I said this on Twitter, and I got a lot of heat for it, but Uncle Vanya is not a play that I particularly love. I certainly don't hate it, but it is never been a play that has really resonated with me. And this production, while being a new adaptation by Amy Hertzog, is a very straightforward adaptation of Uncle Vanya. One of the adaptational choices that they made that I really did like is that they removed the sense of time and place from the show. And so while you're watching the show, you get the sense of this could be happening anywhere at any time. But besides that, this is pretty much your standard Uncle Vanya. And given that this is such a conventional production of Uncle Vanya, I was really surprised by how much I liked it. And of course, a lot of that comes down to this cast, who is just insanely talented across the board. You have Steve Carell, of course, but then you also have William Justin Harper, Nica, Noni Rose, Allison Pill, Alfred Molina. Like, it is just an insanely stacked cast, and I have to say, every single one of them delivers. Think for me, these standouts were Allison Pill and William Jackson Harper. Alison Pill is just giving this incredible, emotionally raw performance at Sonia. And then William Jackson Harper has just mastered that, like Awkward but charming persona. And it works really, really well for his character as well. And then, of course, you have Steve Carell himself, who I thought was really excellent. Now, if you go in expecting the Office Steve Carell, I think you're going to be sorely disappointed. This is not a comedy. Very much more in the vein of Carell's more dramatic works. And there are certainly moments of comedy, and Steve Carell, of course, nails that. He's one of the funniest people alive. But it's all very subtle and grounded comedy. It's not that over the top, almost sketch comedy of the office. And there are some more dramatic moments of this play that I thought he really nailed. There's one in particular where he is crawling on a table and, like, yelling at Alfred Molita. And I was just like, oh, this is good. Like, this is good dramatic acting. I think my one main disappointment would be the physical production, which in general is very sparse. There are a couple of interesting scenic moments which I won't spoil. But honestly, even those I felt like could have packed a bigger punch. So while this is an extremely well acted production, if you swapped out all of those actors, I'm not sure I would like this production as much.
reasoning: Reviewer was pleasantly surprised despite not loving the play, praises the cast extensively, but has reservations about the conventional adaptation and sparse physical production, noting the production relies heavily on its cast.
